author: implementation-agent

findings.summary: Redirect Location paths are resolved with URL before raw path segments are validated.
findings.consequence: A Reader response Location such as /txt/a/%2e%2e/b is normalized to /txt/b before isSafeReaderPath checks it, so the proxy emits a local redirect for a malformed backend path instead of dropping the Location header. This does not escape the allowed Reader prefixes, but it weakens the response-boundary check and can hide backend contract bugs by redirecting to a different asset than the raw Location expressed.
findings.evidence: localReaderRedirect calls new URL(location, target) on line 209, then validates resolved.pathname on line 217. A read-only node URL probe showed /txt/a/%2e%2e/b resolves to pathname /txt/b, which satisfies the current Reader namespace/path checks and would be returned as /txt/b.
findings.recommendation: Validate the raw Location path before URL dot-segment normalization. Split raw path/query/fragment, reject raw or percent-encoded dot segments with the same segment validator, and only then build the returned local redirect from validated raw components.
